title: Homemade Country Bread
instructions:
Homemade Country Bread

Long-fermented country bread baked in a covered pot for a deep crisp crust.

Yield: 1 medium loaf

Ingredients

3 cups bread flour or all-purpose flour
1 1/2 cups cold water
1/4 tsp active dry yeast
2 1/2 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup flour for dusting

Preparation

1. Put the flour, yeast, and salt in a stand-mixer bowl.

2. Mix briefly with the paddle.

3. Slowly add the cold water.

4. Mix into a very soft sticky dough.

5. Alternatively, stir vigorously with a wooden spoon.

6. Cover the bowl well.

7. Ferment in a warm place overnight, about 10–12 hours.

8. Lightly flour the work surface.

9. Turn out the dough gently.

10. Without kneading, fold the edges toward the center and shape into a ball.

11. Flour a clean kitchen towel generously.

12. Put the loaf on the towel.

13. Cover.

14. Proof for 1–2 hours.

15. About 30 minutes before the proof ends, put a covered cast-iron pot in the oven.

16. Preheat the oven and pot to 450°F.

17. Carefully remove the hot pot.

18. Gently invert the dough into the pot.

19. Cover immediately.

20. Bake for 30 minutes.

21. Remove the lid.

22. Continue baking for 15–20 minutes, until deeply golden.

23. Turn the loaf onto a rack.

24. Cool completely before slicing.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The overnight fermentation with very little yeast develops flavor without requiring intensive kneading.

Calabrian Focaccia with ’Nduja and Red Onion

Soft Calabrian focaccia with ’nduja, Tropea red onion, caciocavallo, and oregano.

5. Knead until the dough begins to become smooth.

6. Add the salt.

7. Add the olive oil.

9. Cover.

title: Pane Nero di Castelvetrano
instructions:
Pane Nero di Castelvetrano

Dark Sicilian bread made with local durum-grain flour, long fermentation, and a deeply baked crust.

Yield: 1 large loaf

Ingredients

about 1/2 cup plus 2 tbsp active liquid sourdough starter
1 2/3 cups sparkling water
about 3 cups Castelvetrano black-bread flour blend
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp bread flour
1 tsp diastatic malt powder
2 tbsp water
2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the liquid starter in the mixer bowl.

2. Add the sparkling water.

3. Mix until the starter is completely dispersed.

4. Mix the black-bread flour with the diastatic malt.

5. Add the flour to the liquid.

6. Mix quickly for a few minutes.

7. Cover.

8. Rest for 30 minutes.

9. Sift the bread flour.

10. Add it to the dough.

11. Dissolve the salt in the additional water.

12. Add the salted water.

13. Knead for 10 minutes.

14. Shape into a ball.

15. Put in a covered bowl.

16. Refrigerate for about 20 hours.

17. The next day, leave at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.

18. Turn onto a floured work surface.

19. Fold the edges toward the center.

20. Turn over.

21. Rest for 30 minutes.

22. Repeat the folding and resting process twice more.

23. Shape the loaf.

24. Make one deep vertical slash across the top.

25. Preheat the oven to its highest practical temperature, ideally about 480°F.

26. Bake for 20 minutes at maximum heat.

27. Reduce the oven to 400°F.

28. Bake for 30 minutes.

29. Reduce to 350°F.

30. Bake for another 10 minutes.

31. Cool for at least 2 hours before slicing.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The long refrigerator fermentation develops aroma and structure without requiring a large amount of yeast.

title: Pane di Lentini
instructions:
Pane di Lentini

Sicilian naturally leavened durum-semolina bread shaped into an S and coated with sesame seeds.

Yield: 4 loaves

Ingredients

about 6 2/3 cups finely milled durum semolina
3 cups warm water
about 2 1/4 cups active natural starter
1 tsp honey
4 tsp fine salt
6 tbsp corn oil
1/3 cup sesame seeds

Preparation

1. Refresh the natural starter.

2. Wait until it doubles in volume.

3. Dissolve it in 1 1/2 cups warm water with the honey.

4. Add about half of the semolina.

5. Knead until uniform.

6. Gradually add the remaining semolina.

7. Gradually add the remaining water.

8. Add the corn oil.

9. Add the salt last.

10. Knead for another 5 minutes, until smooth.

11. Shape into a ball.

12. Put in an oiled bowl.

13. Cover with plastic wrap.

14. Let rise for 4–5 hours.

15. Divide into 4 pieces.

16. Round each piece.

17. Cover.

18. Rest for 1 hour.

19. Flatten each piece slightly.

20. Roll into a log.

21. Curve the log into the characteristic S shape.

22. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

23. Cover.

24. Proof for another 2 hours.

25. Preheat a conventional oven to 375°F.

26. Brush the surface with water.

27. Coat generously with sesame seeds.

28. Bake on a low oven rack for 40–45 minutes.

29. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

The S shape increases the crust surface and distinguishes Lentini bread from ordinary Sicilian loaves.

title: Sicilian Mafalda
instructions:
Sicilian Mafalda

Sicilian semolina bread with sesame seeds, shaped into its characteristic looping form.

Yield: 2 loaves

Ingredients

3 cups finely milled durum semolina
1 cup plus 3 tbsp water
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
1 1/2 tsp fine salt
1 tsp malt powder
1/3 cup sesame seeds

Preparation

1. Put the semolina, malt, and yeast in a large bowl.

2. Add about 1 cup water.

3. Knead until well combined.

4. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 2 tablespoons water.

5. Gradually add the salted water.

6. Knead until smooth and elastic.

7. Cover.

8. Rest for 20 minutes.

9. Divide into 2 equal pieces.

10. Round each piece.

11. Cover.

12. Proof for 60 minutes.

13. Roll each piece into a rope about 32 inches long.

14. Arrange the rope on the baking sheet in 3–4 parallel curves.

15. Bring the final end over the center of the shape.

16. Lightly wet the surface with water.

17. Coat with sesame seeds.

18. Cover.

19. Proof for another 60 minutes.

20. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

21. Bake for 40–45 minutes, until deeply golden.

22. Cool on a rack.

Chef's note

Keep the rope an even thickness so every curve of the mafalda bakes at the same rate.

Preparation

1. Put the semolina in a very large bowl.

2. Add the softened lard and yeast.

3. Mix.

4. Make a well in the center.

5. Add the eggs one at a time.

6. Add the salt.

7. Add the warm milk.

8. Gradually add the warm water.

9. Knead vigorously into a very soft sticky dough.

10. Mix in about half of the elderflowers.

11. Cover.

12. Let rise for about 1 hour, until doubled.

13. Brown the pancetta in a dry skillet for 4–5 minutes.

14. Drain excess rendered fat.

15. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

16. Grease a large deep round pan with the lard.

17. Divide the dough in half.

18. Spread half over the bottom with a spoon or oiled hands.

19. Leave about a 3/4-inch border.

20. Layer with the tuma, salami, and pancetta.

21. Scatter some of the remaining elderflowers over the filling.

22. Cover with the remaining dough.

23. Scatter the remaining elderflowers over the top.

24. Cover.

25. Rest for 30 minutes.

26. Bake for 45–50 minutes, until well risen and golden.

27. Cool for at least 15 minutes before cutting.

Serve hot or warm.

The traditional dough is intentionally very soft; use oiled hands rather than adding extra flour.

instructions:
Sfincione Palermitano

Soft Palermo sfincione topped with onion, tomato, anchovy, and caciocavallo.

Yield: 1 large pan, about 8 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
5 3/4 cups all-purpose flour
1 3/4 cups fine durum semolina

about 2 tbsp fresh yeast or 2 1/2 tsp dry yeast

about 3/4 cup oil-packed anchovy fillets, optional

Preparation

1. Mix the all-purpose flour and semolina in a large bowl.

2. Add the salt.

3. Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water.

4. Pour the liquid into the flours.

5. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil.

6. Knead vigorously for at least 15 minutes until very soft and elastic.

7. Cover.

8. Let rise for 2–3 hours.

9. Thinly slice the onions.

10. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan.

11. Add the onions.

12. Cook for 5 minutes.

13. Add 1/2 cup water.

15. Add the crushed peeled tomatoes.

16. Add the salt.

17. Cover and cook over low heat for 30 minutes.

18. Grease a baking pan with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil.

19. Sprinkle half of the breadcrumbs over the base.

20. Press the dough into the pan with oiled hands.

21. Scatter over the anchovies if using.

22. Add the fresh caciocavallo.

23. Let rise for another 30 minutes.

24. Cover with the onion-tomato sauce.

25. Add the grated semi-aged caciocavallo.

26. Sprinkle with the remaining breadcrumbs.

27. Drizzle with any remaining topping oil.

28. Bake in a preheated 480°F oven for about 20 minutes.

29. Finish with oregano immediately after baking.

Service

Serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

The dough should remain very soft because sfincione is defined by its high, airy, sponge-like crumb.

title: Sfincione Bagherese
instructions:
Sfincione Bagherese

Bagheria white sfincione with onions, ricotta, tuma, anchovies, and seasoned breadcrumbs.

Yield: 1 large pan, about 8 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
3 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 cup fine durum semolina
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 tbsp granulated sugar
2 tsp fine salt
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
1 cup water

For the topping
3 white onions
10 anchovy fillets
1 2/3 cups sheep's-milk ricotta
2 1/2 cups diced tuma cheese
1/3 cup grated caciocavallo
about 2 cups fresh breadcrumbs
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 tsp dried oregano

Preparation

1. Mix the all-purpose flour, semolina, yeast, and sugar.

2. Add the olive oil.

3. Gradually add the water.

4. Add the salt.

5. Knead until smooth and elastic.

6. Cover.

7. Let rise for about 3 hours.

8. Thinly slice the onions.

9. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet.

10. Melt 3 anchovy fillets into the oil.

11. Add the onions.

12. Season with half of the salt and the pepper.

13. Cover and cook over medium-low heat until very soft.

14. Cool.

15. Crumble the bread.

16. Toast it briefly in a skillet with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

17. Add the caciocavallo and 1 teaspoon oregano.

18. Cool.

19. Grease a baking pan with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil.

20. Press the dough into the pan.

21. Scatter the remaining anchovies over the dough.

22. Add the tuma.

23. Spoon over the ricotta.

24. Cover with the onions.

25. Sprinkle with the seasoned breadcrumbs.

26. Let rise for another hour.

27. Finish with the remaining salt and oregano.

28. Bake in a preheated 400°F conventional oven for about 30 minutes.

Service

Serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

Bagheria sfincione is intentionally white; sweet onions, ricotta, tuma, and toasted crumbs replace the tomato topping.

title: Pane Carasau
instructions:
Pane Carasau

Ultra-thin Sardinian bread baked twice until crisp.

Yield: about 8–10 sheets

Ingredients

2 1/3 cups fine durum semolina
1 cup water
1 tsp fresh yeast
2/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in part of the warm water.

2. Make a well in the semolina.

3. Add the salt.

4. Add the dissolved yeast.

5. Gradually add the remaining water.

6. Knead until smooth and elastic.

7. Divide into equal small balls.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise for about 3 hours.

10. Roll each ball into a very thin disk about 12 inches wide.

11. Heat a baking sheet in a 425°F oven.

12. Bake one disk at a time for about 20 seconds, until it balloons into two layers.

13. Remove immediately.

14. Carefully separate the two layers while still hot.

15. Arrange them on separate baking sheets.

16. Reduce the oven to 350°F.

17. Bake the sheets for about 8 minutes, until dry and golden.

18. Cool completely.

Service

Serve crisp or rehydrate according to the intended dish.

Chef's note

Separate the layers immediately after the bread puffs; once cool, they are much harder to divide without breaking.

title: Pane Guttiau
instructions:
Pane Guttiau

Pane carasau brushed with extra-virgin olive oil, salt, and rosemary, then toasted again.

Yield: about 8–10 sheets

Ingredients

For the bread
2 1/3 cups fine durum semolina
1 cup water
1 tsp fresh yeast
2/3 tsp fine salt

For seasoning
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/2 tsp fine salt
1 tsp finely chopped fresh rosemary

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in a little warm water.

2. Make a well in the semolina.

3. Add the salt.

4. Add the dissolved yeast.

5. Gradually add the remaining water.

6. Knead until elastic.

7. Cover.

8. Rest for 15 minutes.

9. Divide into equal balls.

10. Dust with semolina.

11. Cover and let rise for about 3 hours.

12. Roll each ball into a thin disk.

13. Rest the disks covered for 30 minutes.

14. Bake in a very hot oven until each disk puffs.

15. Immediately separate the two layers.

16. Toast the sheets on both sides until dry.

17. Mix the olive oil, salt, and rosemary.

18. Brush each sheet lightly.

19. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

20. Bake again for 2–3 minutes, until crisp and lightly golden.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Brush on only a thin film of oil; too much softens the bread instead of keeping it crisp.

title: Civraxiu
instructions:
Civraxiu

Large Campidano sourdough bread made with durum semolina and wheat flour.

Yield: 2 large loaves

Ingredients

5 cups fine durum semolina
1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
about 1 cup active sourdough starter
2–3 cups water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Refresh the sourdough starter.

2. Let it mature for about 8 hours.

3. Put the semolina, flour, and salt in the mixer.

4. Mix dry for 10 minutes.

5. Add 2 cups water.

6. Knead until the dough begins pulling away from the bowl.

7. Add the sourdough starter.

8. Continue kneading for another 10 minutes.

9. Gradually add more water, up to a total of 3 cups, only until the dough is soft but still structured.

10. Rest in the mixer bowl for 15 minutes.

11. Divide into two large portions.

12. Shape gently.

13. Cover.

14. Let rise at about 79–81°F for roughly 3 hours, until at least doubled.

15. Gently reshape.

16. Put into floured cloth-lined proofing baskets.

17. Proof for another 2–3 hours.

18. Preheat the oven to 480°F.

19. Load the loaves.

20. Bake for about 30 minutes at 465–480°F.

21. Reduce the oven to 390°F.

22. Continue baking for another 30 minutes.

23. Remove from the oven.

24. Cover the loaves with a clean towel while cooling.

Service

Cool completely before slicing.

Chef's note

Add the water gradually; Civraxiu should be well hydrated while still strong enough to support a large loaf.

title: Coccoi a Pitzus
instructions:
Coccoi a Pitzus

Firm Sardinian semolina bread decorated with the characteristic pitzus cuts.

Yield: 3–4 decorated loaves

Ingredients

5 3/4 cups fine durum semolina
1 3/4 cups plus 2 tbsp water
about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Warm 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon of the water.

2. Dissolve the yeast in it.

3. Put the semolina in a large bowl.

4. Gradually add the remaining water.

5. Add the dissolved yeast.

6. Add the salt.

7. Knead thoroughly until very elastic and firm.

8. Cover.

9. Rest for about 1 hour.

10. Divide into portions of roughly 1 1/2 cups dough each.

11. Shape each loaf as desired.

12. Create the traditional decorative cuts with scissors or a razor.

13. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

14. Cover with plastic wrap.

15. Proof in a turned-off oven with the light on for at least 5–6 hours.

16. Put a small pan of water on the oven floor.

17. Preheat the oven to its maximum temperature.

18. Load the loaves.

19. Bake for 10 minutes at maximum heat.

20. Reduce the oven to 400°F.

21. Continue baking for about 20 minutes.

22. Turn off the oven.

23. Cool on a rack with the oven door slightly open.

Service

Serve completely cooled.

Chef's note

The dough should remain firm so the decorative cuts stay sharp during the long proof and baking.

title: Moddizzosu
instructions:
Moddizzosu

Soft Campidano bread made with durum semolina, durum flour, and sourdough starter.

Yield: 1 large loaf

Ingredients

3 cups fine durum semolina
2 1/2 cups durum flour
1 2/3 cups durum flour for the preferment
about 1/3 cup active sourdough starter
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water, divided
2 tbsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Refresh the sourdough starter.

2. Let it mature.

3. Make the preferment by mixing the starter with 1 2/3 cups flour and a scant 1/2 cup water.

4. Cover.

5. Ferment in a warm place for several hours, preferably overnight.

6. Put the semolina and remaining durum flour in a large bowl.

7. Add the mature preferment.

8. Gradually add the remaining water.

9. Knead vigorously.

10. Add the salt only after the dough begins coming together.

11. Continue kneading until smooth, elastic, and well developed.

12. Shape into a round loaf.

13. Cover.

14. Let rise until doubled.

15. Preheat the oven to 445°F with a baking stone or heavy sheet if available.

16. Score the loaf.

17. Load the bread.

18. Bake for about 15 minutes at 445°F.

19. Reduce the oven to 400°F.

20. Continue baking for 35–45 minutes, until deeply golden and hollow-sounding underneath.

21. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Chef's note

The sourdough preferment develops the aroma and soft crumb characteristic of Moddizzosu.

Pistoccu

Thin crisp Sardinian bread that is leavened and baked twice.

Yield: about 8–10 sheets

4 cups durum flour
about 1 tbsp sourdough starter
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
2 cups plus 2 tbsp warm water

Preparation

1. Put the semolina and durum flour in a large bowl.

2. Dissolve the salt in the warm water.

3. Add the sourdough starter to the flours.

4. Gradually add the salted water.

5. Knead until smooth and elastic.

6. Divide into equal small loaves.

7. Cover.

8. Rest for 20 minutes.

9. Roll each piece into a sheet about 12 inches wide and 1/8 inch thick.

10. Dust with semolina.

11. Cover.

12. Proof for 2–3 hours.

13. Preheat the oven to 480°F.

14. Bake one sheet at a time until it puffs.

15. Remove immediately.

16. Separate the two layers.

17. Cool under a light weight to keep them flat.

18. Return the sheets to the oven.

19. Bake again until dry and golden.

20. Cool completely.

Service

Serve crisp or lightly rehydrate with water before use.

Chef's note

The second bake removes residual moisture and gives Pistoccu its long keeping quality.

Spianata Sarda

Thin soft Sardinian semolina bread made with sourdough.

1 1/2 cups fine durum semolina
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water
about 1 cup sourdough starter or 2 tsp fresh yeast
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put both semolinas in a large bowl.

2. Add the sourdough starter.

3. Add about 1 2/3 cups water.

4. Knead for several minutes.

5. Dissolve the salt in the remaining water.

6. Gradually add the salted water.

7. Continue kneading until smooth.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise for 1 hour.

10. Divide into portions of about 2/3 cup dough each.

11. Round them.

12. Cover.

13. Let rise for 40 minutes.

14. Roll each portion into a disk no more than 3/16 inch thick.

15. Cover.

16. Rest for 1 hour.

17. Preheat the oven to 480°F with a baking stone or heavy sheet inside.

18. Bake the flatbreads for 6 minutes total.

19. Turn halfway through.

20. Cool covered with a towel to keep them soft.

Service

Chef's note

Unlike carasau, spianata should remain soft, so do not extend the bake beyond what is necessary.

Pane di Ozieri

Soft thin Ozieri flatbread made with durum semolina, sourdough, water, and salt.

Ingredients

about 5 3/4 cups durum semolina
about 1 cup active sourdough starter
1 2/3 cups warm water
1 1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Reserve about 1 1/4 cups of the flour.

2. Dissolve the sourdough starter in a scant 1/2 cup warm water.

3. Add the reserved flour.

4. Knead into a small dough ball.

5. Dust lightly with flour.

6. Cover.

7. Ferment for about 3 hours in a warm place.

8. Put the remaining flour in a large bowl.

9. Add the fermented starter dough.

10. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 1 1/4 cups water.

11. Gradually add the salted water.

12. Knead vigorously for an extended period until elastic and compact.

13. Divide into 8 portions.

14. Shape into balls.

15. Cover.

16. Rest for 30 minutes.

17. Roll each ball into a disk about 10–12 inches wide and only a few millimeters thick.

18. Decorate with a traditional pintadera if desired.

19. Preheat the oven to 480°F with a heavy baking sheet inside.

20. Bake each flatbread for about 8–10 minutes, until only lightly colored and still soft.

21. Cool covered with a towel.

Serve soft with cheese, cured meats, soups, or roasted meats.

Chef's note

Ozieri flatbread should remain flexible; roll it thin and bake quickly so it does not dry out.

Neapolitan Pane Cafone

Neapolitan sourdough country bread with a dark crust and elastic crumb.

5. Add the starter mixture.

7. Add the remaining flour.

8. Add the salt.

18. Bake with steam for the first 10 minutes.

20. Reduce the oven to 410°F.

Pane cafone needs a deeply developed crust and full fermentation, so do not shorten the final proof.

title: Pane dei Camaldoli
instructions:
Pane dei Camaldoli

Long-fermented Neapolitan bread made with a highly hydrated dough.

Yield: 1 loaf

Ingredients

5 cups all-purpose or type 0 flour
1 2/3 cups water
2 1/4 tsp fine salt
about 1/4 tsp fresh yeast

Preparation

1. Put the flour, yeast, water, and salt in a large bowl.

2. Mix quickly with a fork.

3. Stop when no dry flour remains; the dough should stay rough and sticky.

4. Cover tightly with plastic wrap.

5. Ferment at room temperature for at least 24 hours.

6. Using a spatula, make 4–5 folds directly in the bowl.

7. Cover again.

8. Let rise for another 2 hours.

9. Preheat the oven to 425°F with a covered clay pot or Dutch oven inside.

10. Carefully turn the dough into the hot pot.

11. Cover.

12. Bake for 40 minutes.

13. Remove the lid.

14. Continue baking for another 20 minutes, until deeply browned.

15. Remove from the pot.

16. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Chef's note

The 24-hour fermentation develops flavor and structure without intensive kneading.

Sardinian Pardulas

18. Pinch the edge in 5–6 places to create a star shape.

6. Add the sourdough starter.

7. Knead in the bowl until evenly distributed.

8. Add the salt.

9. Continue kneading until uniform.

10. Cover.

11. Rest for about 2 hours.

12. Turn onto a floured work surface.

15. Cover.

The initial autolyse helps Saragolla flour absorb water and develop elasticity before the sourdough is added.

19. Reduce the oven to 300°F.

20. Arrange cut-side up.

21. Bake for 30–40 minutes, turning halfway through, until completely dry and crisp.

22. Cool completely.

Service

Briefly soak with water before topping, or serve crisp.

Chef's note

The second bake should remove nearly all moisture; that is what gives freselle their long keeping quality and crunch.

Neapolitan Casatiello

Neapolitan Easter ring bread filled with cured meats and cheeses and decorated with whole eggs.

2. Put the flour in a large bowl.

8. Cover.

14. Roll tightly.

20. Arrange them on top.

23. Bake for about 50 minutes.

24. Cool until warm in the mold.

The decorative eggs bake with the bread, so use only clean eggs with completely intact shells.

Neapolitan Tortano

Neapolitan ring bread filled with salami, pancetta, provolone, Pecorino, and hard-boiled eggs.

For the dough
4 1/2 cups bread flour

about 1 2/3 cups diced sharp provolone
about 1 1/3 cups diced salami
about 3/4 cup diced pancetta

3 large eggs

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

2. Pour the liquid into a mixer bowl.

3. Add the flour, first portion of Pecorino, and pepper.

4. Begin kneading.

5. Add the salt.

6. Add the lard little by little.

7. Continue kneading for about 15 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise in a warm place until doubled.

10. Boil the eggs for 8 minutes.

11. Cool.

12. Peel.

13. Cut the eggs, provolone, salami, and pancetta into pieces.

14. Roll the dough into a large rectangle.

15. Spread the filling evenly.

16. Sprinkle with the remaining Pecorino.

17. Roll tightly.

18. Put into a 10-inch ring mold.

19. Join the ends securely.

20. Cover.

21. Let rise again until well expanded.

22. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

23. Bake for 60 minutes.

24. Cool until warm.

25. Unmold.

In tortano, the eggs are hard-boiled and enclosed in the filling, unlike casatiello where whole eggs are displayed on top.

instructions:
Pizza di Scarola

Neapolitan pizza topped with escarole, Gaeta olives, capers, anchovies, raisins, and pine nuts.

Yield: 2 pizzas, about 16 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
4 cups bread flour
3/4 cup fine durum semolina
1 1/2 cups plus 1 tbsp water
about 1 tbsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided

For the topping
about 8 cups chopped escarole
1/3 cup raisins
1/3 cup pine nuts
10 pitted Gaeta olives
1 tbsp rinsed capers
4 oil-packed anchovy fillets
1 garlic clove
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Mix the bread flour and semolina.

2. Add the crumbled yeast.

3. Add the water.

4. Add the salt.

5. Knead into a soft dough.

6. Cover.

7. Let rise for 1–2 hours, until doubled.

8. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

9. Drain and squeeze dry.

10. Divide the dough in half.

11. Stretch into two round pans about 10 and 12 inches wide.

12. Whisk 2 tablespoons olive oil with 1 tablespoon water.

13. Brush over the dough.

14. Rest for 15–20 minutes.

15. Wash and tear the escarole.

16. Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a skillet.

17. Add the garlic.

18. Add the raisins, capers, and olives.

19. Cook for 1 minute.

20. Add the escarole.

21. Add the salt.

22. Toss for 30–60 seconds, only until slightly wilted.

23. Spread over the pizzas.

24. Bake in a preheated 400°F oven for about 20 minutes.

25. Toast the pine nuts.

26. Finish the pizzas with the anchovies and pine nuts.

Service

Serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

Keep the escarole relatively dry; an overly wet topping makes the crust soft.

Pizza Chiena

Campania filled pie with cheese, cured meats, eggs, and Parmigiano.

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water.

2. Put the flour in a large bowl.

11. Add the Parmigiano.

12. Divide the dough into two portions, one slightly larger.

13. Roll out the larger portion.

14. Line a 9 1/2–10-inch pan.

15. Add the cheeses and cured meats.

16. Pour the egg-and-Parmigiano mixture over them.

17. Roll out the remaining dough.

18. Cover the pie.

title: Genzano Country Bread
instructions:
Genzano Country Bread

Genzano sourdough country bread with a dark wheat-bran-coated crust.

Yield: 1 large loaf

2 cups water, divided
about 3/4 cup active sourdough starter
2 1/4 tsp fine salt
about 1/3 cup wheat bran

Preparation

1. Put about 1 3/4 cups plus 2 tablespoons water in a large bowl.

2. Add the sourdough starter.

3. Stir until dispersed.

4. Gradually mix in the flour.

5. Cover.

6. Rest for 20 minutes.

7. Dissolve the salt in the remaining water.

8. Gradually work in the salted water.

9. Knead for 8–10 minutes.

10. Cover.

11. Rest for 30 minutes.

12. Make a set of folds from all four sides.

13. Continue fermenting until well expanded.

14. Shape into a loaf.

15. Spread the wheat bran on a cloth or proofing basket.

16. Roll or set the loaf surface against the bran to coat it.

17. Proof until well developed.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 465°F with a baking stone or heavy sheet.

19. Create steam in the oven.

20. Load the bread.

21. Bake for 15 minutes at 465°F with steam.

22. Remove the steam source.

23. Reduce the oven to 410°F.

24. Continue baking for 30–35 minutes.

25. Cool completely on a rack.

Chef's note

The wheat-bran coating contributes to the thick, dark, aromatic crust characteristic of Genzano bread.

Pane di Lariano

Lazio country bread made with whole-wheat flour, type 0 flour, and a long fermentation.

2 cups all-purpose or type 0 flour
1 3/4 cups water, divided

2 tsp fine salt
1 tsp honey

Preparation

1. Pour about 1 1/2 cups plus 1 tablespoon water into a large bowl.

2. Add the yeast.

3. Add the honey.

4. Stir until the yeast dissolves.

5. Add the whole-wheat flour and type 0 flour.

6. Knead until all of the flour is hydrated.

7. Dissolve the salt in the remaining water.

8. Gradually work in the salted water.

9. Knead for about 10 minutes.

10. Shape into a ball.

11. Cover.

12. Rest for 20 minutes.

13. Make one set of folds.

14. Rest another 20 minutes.

15. Repeat the folds a second time.

16. Let rise until well expanded.

17. Shape into a loaf.

18. Dust with the handling whole-wheat flour.

19. Proof again.

20. Preheat a conventional oven to 445°F for at least 30 minutes.

21. Score the surface.

22. Create steam in the oven.

23. Bake for 15 minutes at 445°F.

24. Remove the steam source.

25. Reduce the oven to 390°F.

26. Continue baking for 30–35 minutes.

27. Cool completely on a rack.

The spaced folding steps strengthen the dough without aggressive kneading.

Roman Pizza Bianca

Roman-style pizza bianca baked in long slabs, crisp outside and highly aerated inside.

Yield: 3 slabs, about 2 cups dough each

scant 1 cup cold water
scant 1/2 cup additional cold water

about 1/2 tsp fresh yeast

about 2/3 cup semolina for dusting

Preparation

2. Mix only until the flour is hydrated.

3. Cover.

4. Rest for 1 hour.

5. Add the yeast and malt.

6. Begin kneading.

7. Gradually add the remaining water.

8. Once the dough has formed, add the salt.

9. Add the olive oil.

10. Continue until fully developed.

11. Make one set of folds.

12. Let rise until well expanded.

13. Divide into 3 equal portions.

14. Shape gently.

15. Rest covered.

16. Preheat a conventional oven to 480°F with a baking stone or heavy sheet.

17. Dust the work surface generously with semolina.

18. Stretch each piece into a long slab without crushing the air pockets.

19. Transfer to parchment or a peel.

20. Drizzle each slab with 2 teaspoons olive oil.

21. Sprinkle each with about 1/3 teaspoon salt.

22. Bake on a low oven rack for 10–12 minutes.

23. Cool briefly on a rack.

During stretching, push the air toward the edges rather than flattening the dough; open crumb is essential to Roman pizza bianca.

Falia di Priverno

scant 1 cup water

White Bread

1/2 cup warm whole milk

1. Pour the warm milk and water into a stand-mixer bowl.

2. Add the flour, yeast, salt, egg, and olive oil.

4. Knead on low speed for about 15 minutes.

5. Stop when smooth and elastic.

6. Transfer to a lightly oiled bowl.

7. Cover.

8. Let rise for about 60 minutes, until doubled.

9. Line a baking sheet with parchment.

10. Roll the dough into a rectangle about 10 × 16 inches.

11. Roll tightly from a long side into a log.

12. Seal the seam.

13. Cut lengthwise down the center, leaving about 2 inches intact at both ends.

14. Twist the two cut sections so the inner layers face upward.

15. Put on the baking sheet.

Torta al Testo

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp baking soda
1 cup warm water
3 tbsp Umbrian extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

1. Mix the flour, salt, and baking soda.

2. Make a well.

3. Add the olive oil.

4. Gradually add the warm water.

5. Knead vigorously for 8–10 minutes.

6. Stop when smooth and nonsticky.

7. Divide into 4 portions.

8. Shape into balls.

9. Roll each into a disk about 10–11 inches wide and 3/16 inch thick.

10. Heat a traditional testo or heavy griddle for at least 10 minutes.

11. Put one disk on the hot surface.

12. Cook for 8–10 minutes over medium heat.

13. Turn.

Umbrian naturally leavened bread, traditionally nearly unsalted, with a wheat-bran-dusted crust.

Tuscan Unsalted Bread

Traditional Tuscan saltless sourdough bread with a long fermentation.

about 2 tbsp sourdough starter

For the dough
8 1/3 cups all-purpose flour

about 1 cup sourdough starter
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the container

Preparation

1. The night before, mix the strong flour, water, and starter.

2. Cover.

3. Ferment for 10–12 hours.

4. The next day, put the water in the mixer.

5. Add the preferment.

6. Add the remaining sourdough starter.

7. Mix for 30–40 seconds.

8. Add the flour.

9. Knead for 15–18 minutes, until smooth.

10. Lightly oil a container.

11. Transfer the dough.

12. Cover.

13. Let rise for 90 minutes at 79–82°F.

15. Cover.

20. Proof for another 2 hours.

21. Preheat the oven to 425°F.

23. Bake for 15 minutes at 425°F, spraying water during the first 5 minutes.

24. Reduce the oven to 390°F.

25. Bake for 20 minutes.

26. Reduce to 350°F.

27. Continue for another 10–15 minutes.

28. Cool completely on a rack.

Service

Slice at room temperature.

Traditional Tuscan bread contains no salt; its flavor comes from fermentation, wheat, and crust development.

The long preferment maturation gives Altopascio bread its characteristic aroma and structure.

instructions:
Tuscan Schiacciata

Soft olive-oil-rich Tuscan flatbread made with a 12-hour preferment.

Ingredients

2 cups bread flour
1 cup warm water
1/4 tsp active dry yeast

For the final dough
about 2 cups prepared preferment
4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 cup water
1 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

For the pan and top
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2/3 tsp coarse salt

Preparation

1. The night before, mix the preferment flour, water, and yeast.

2. Cover.

3. Ferment for about 12 hours.

4. The next day, transfer the preferment to a large bowl.

5. Add the flour, water, and salt.

6. Knead into a very soft sticky dough.

7. Grease a large baking pan with about 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil.

8. Transfer the dough to the pan.

9. Gently stretch it with your fingers.

10. If it springs back, wait 10 minutes and continue stretching.

11. Cover.

12. Proof in the pan for about 2 hours.

13. Preheat the oven to 400°F.

14. Press deep dimples with your fingertips.

15. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

16. Sprinkle with the coarse salt.

17. Bake for 20–25 minutes, until deeply golden.

18. Cool briefly on a rack.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Letting the dough relax between stretches prevents tearing the gluten structure.

15. Lightly crush some grapes with a fork.

16. Sprinkle with about half of the remaining sugar.

17. Roll or stretch the remaining dough.

18. Cover the first layer.

19. Add the remaining grapes.

20. Sprinkle with the remaining sugar.

21. Drizzle with the final 1 tablespoon olive oil.

title: Pane di Chiaserna
instructions:
Pane di Chiaserna

Marche country loaf with a long fermentation and a crisp, deeply baked crust.

Yield: 1 large loaf, about 2 lb

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or bread flour
1 1/2 cups room-temperature water, divided
1 tsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp flour for the work surface
scant 1/2 cup boiling water for oven steam

Preparation

1. Pour about 1 1/3 cups water into a large bowl.

2. Dissolve the yeast in it.

3. Gradually add the flour, mixing first with a spoon and then by hand.

4. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 2 tablespoons water.

5. Gradually work the salted water into the dough.

6. Knead until soft, elastic, and slightly sticky.

7. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

8. With lightly damp hands, stretch one edge of the dough and fold it toward the center.

9. Rotate the bowl and repeat on all four sides.

10. Cover and wait 30 minutes.

11. Repeat the folding sequence twice more at 30-minute intervals.

12. After the final folds, cover and rise for 3–4 hours, until puffy and filled with small bubbles.

13. Dust the work surface with the measured flour.

14. Turn out the dough gently and spread it without deflating it.

15. Fold the edges toward the center.

16. Turn seam-side down and gently tighten into a round loaf.

17. Put it seam-side up in a floured proofing basket.

18. Cover and rise for 1 1/2–2 hours.

19. Preheat a conventional oven to 465°F for at least 30 minutes with a heavy baking sheet or stone inside and a small metal pan on the bottom rack.

20. Turn the loaf onto parchment.

21. Score the surface with a sharp blade.

22. Transfer to the preheated baking surface.

23. Pour the boiling water into the lower pan and immediately close the oven.

24. Bake at 465°F for 15 minutes.

25. Carefully remove the steam pan.

26. Reduce the oven to 410°F.

27. Bake for another 30–35 minutes.

28. Leave the oven door slightly ajar during the final 5 minutes.

29. Cool completely on a rack before slicing.

Chef's note

The folding schedule strengthens the dough without adding excess flour, preserving hydration and a softer crumb.

Marche Easter Cheese Bread

title: Solina Bread
instructions:
Solina Bread

Abruzzo naturally leavened loaf made with ancient Solina wheat flour.

Yield: 1 loaf

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups plus 1 tbsp water
5 cups Solina wheat flour
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

1. Put the refreshed starter and water in the mixer bowl.

2. Whisk until the starter is well dispersed and slightly foamy.

3. Switch to the dough hook.

4. Add the Solina flour and salt.

5. Mix on low speed.

6. After 3–4 minutes, gradually add the olive oil.

7. Continue kneading for 10–15 minutes.

8. Dust the work surface with half of the semolina.

9. Turn out the dough and work it briefly.

10. Put it in a bowl.

11. Cover with a damp kitchen towel.

12. Rest at room temperature for 1–2 hours.

13. Cover securely and refrigerate for about 18 hours.

14. Return to room temperature for 2 hours.

15. Dust the work surface with the remaining semolina.

16. Shape gently into a loaf without aggressively deflating the dough.

17. Cover and complete the final rise for about 1 hour.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 480°F.

19. Score the loaf.

20. Bake at 480°F for 15 minutes.

21. Reduce the oven to 410–425°F.

22. Bake for about 30 minutes more, until the crust is well developed.

23. Cool completely on a rack.

Chef's note

Solina develops a less elastic gluten network than modern wheat, so shape gently rather than trying to force a highly open crumb.

13. Cool for 5 minutes.

Chef's note

Thickness is critical. Because there is no yeast, an overly thick pizza would remain heavy rather than crisp.

Senatore Cappelli Sourdough Bread

Naturally leavened bread made with Senatore Cappelli durum wheat and a long cold fermentation.

Yield: 2 loaves

Ingredients

5 cups Senatore Cappelli durum wheat flour
2 cups plus 3 tbsp water
about 1 cup refreshed sourdough starter
2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Refresh the sourdough starter and let it double.

2. Put all of the flour and water in a bowl.

3. Mix only until no dry flour remains.

4. Cover and autolyse for 1 hour.

5. Add the starter in pieces.

6. Knead until evenly incorporated.

7. Rest for 30 minutes.

8. Add the salt with lightly damp hands.

9. Knead until fully absorbed.

10. Rest for another 30 minutes.

11. Perform one complete set of stretch-and-folds in the bowl.

12. Cover.

13. Refrigerate at about 45°F for 10 hours.

14. Divide the dough into two equal pieces.

15. Shape gently into two loaves.

16. Put them in floured proofing baskets.

17. Cover.

18. Refrigerate for 12 hours.

19. Put a covered Dutch oven in the oven.

20. Preheat to 445°F for at least 30 minutes.

21. Turn one loaf onto parchment.

22. Score with a sharp blade.

23. Transfer to the hot Dutch oven.

24. Cover.

25. Bake for 30 minutes at 445°F.

26. Remove the lid.

27. Reduce the oven to 410°F.

28. Bake for another 20 minutes.

29. Repeat with the second loaf.

30. Cool on a rack for at least 2 hours before slicing.

Chef's note

The high hydration is intentional. Do not add extra flour during handling, because doing so would change the intended crumb structure.

Abruzzo Easter Sweet Bread

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

2. Drain and dry very thoroughly.

3. Beat the 6 eggs with the sugar until pale and foamy.

4. Separately beat the 2 egg whites to soft peaks.

5. Fold the egg whites into the egg mixture.

6. Add the mature sourdough starter and olive oil.

7. Mix until the starter is evenly distributed.

8. Gradually add the flour.

9. Work until the dough is very soft but not liquid.

10. Cover with a clean cloth.

11. Rise in a warm place for about 24 hours.

12. Add the anise seeds, raisins, citron, candied cherries, lemon zest, cinnamon, and chocolate.

13. Knead gently until evenly distributed.

14. Grease a tall baking mold with the measured olive oil.

15. Transfer the dough to the mold.

20. Cool in the mold for 15 minutes.

This traditional bread relies on a very long fermentation. Use a mature, vigorous sourdough starter strong enough to lift a dough rich in eggs and sugar.

instructions:
Abruzzo Parrozzo

Dome-shaped Abruzzo almond cake covered completely in dark chocolate.

Yield: 6–8 servings

Ingredients

2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder for the mold
3/4 cup blanched almonds
1/2 cup cornstarch
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
5 large eggs, separated
1 tsp vanilla extract
2/3 cup sugar
about 1 1/4 cups chopped dark chocolate

Preparation

1. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

2. Butter a dome mold with the softened butter.

3. Coat it evenly with cocoa powder.

4. Finely grind the almonds.

5. Sift together the flour and cornstarch.

6. Beat the egg yolks with the vanilla and sugar until pale and very fluffy.

7. Mix in the melted butter.

8. Add the ground almonds.

9. Fold in the sifted flour and cornstarch.

10. Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks.

11. Fold them in gently in three additions.

12. Pour into the prepared mold.

13. Bake for about 40 minutes.

14. Test the center with a skewer.

15. Cool in the mold for 15 minutes.

16. Unmold onto a rack.

17. Cool completely.

18. Melt the chocolate over a water bath or in short microwave intervals.

19. Cool it for 3–5 minutes.

20. Pour over the dome, completely coating the top and sides.

21. Let the coating set at room temperature.

Chef's note

The beaten egg whites provide the cake's primary aeration, so gentle folding matters more than prolonged mixing.

Molise Cornmeal Flatbread

title: Piadina Romagnola

Piadina Romagnola

Ingredients

1 cup plus 1 tbsp room-temperature water

Preparation

1. Put the flour in a bowl.

2. Add the lard in small pieces.

3. Rub it into the flour with your fingertips.

4. Add the baking soda if using.

5. Gradually add the water.

6. Add the salt.

7. Knead for 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

8. Divide into 6 portions.

9. Shape into balls.

11. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

12. Lightly dust the work surface with the measured flour.

13. Roll each ball into a thin round about 9 inches wide.

15. Cook one flatbread at a time for about 2 minutes on the first side.

16. Turn when bubbles and golden spots appear.

17. Cook the second side for another 1–2 minutes.

title: Crescione Romagnolo
instructions:
Crescione Romagnolo

Romagna half-moon flatbreads filled with creamy Certosa cheese and cooked ham, cooked on a griddle.

Yield: 8 crescioni

Ingredients

For the dough
2 cups type 1 or all-purpose flour
scant 1/2 cup room-temperature water

1 tsp baking soda
3/4 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 2 cups Certosa or soft spreadable cheese
about 1 1/4 cups thinly sliced cooked ham

Preparation

1. Mix the flour and baking soda.

2. Add the lard.

3. Rub it into the flour with your fingertips.

4. Gradually add the water.

5. Add the salt.

6. Knead until smooth.

7. Form a compact ball.

8. Cover with plastic wrap.

9. Rest for at least 30 minutes.

10. Divide into 8 equal portions.

11. Roll each portion into a thin round.

12. Spread about 2 tablespoons Certosa over one half of each round.

13. Add about 2 tablespoons cooked ham.

14. Leave a border about 3/8 inch wide.

15. Fold the empty half over the filling to make a half-moon.

16. Press the edges firmly.

17. Seal with the tines of a fork.

18. Heat a heavy nonstick skillet over medium heat.

19. Cook each crescione for 3–4 minutes per side.

20. Briefly cook the curved edge as well, holding the crescione upright with tongs.

Chef's note

Do not overfill. An overly full crescione tends to split once the cheese melts.

title: Gnocco Fritto
instructions:
Gnocco Fritto

Emilia-style yeasted dough made with milk and lard, fried until puffed and golden.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

2 cups all-purpose flour
scant 1/2 cup whole milk
about 2 1/4 tsp fresh yeast
2 tbsp lard
1/2 tsp fine salt
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying

Preparation

1. Warm the milk to about 82–86°F.

2. Pour it into a bowl.

3. Dissolve the yeast in the milk.

4. Rest for 10 minutes.

5. Add the flour.

6. Add the softened lard.

7. Add the salt.

8. Knead for about 10 minutes by hand, or 3–4 minutes in a stand mixer.

9. Form a ball.

10. Cover.

11. Let rise for 1 hour.

12. Roll the dough to about 1/8 inch thick.

13. Cut into diamonds 2 1/2–3 inches wide.

14. Heat the oil to 375°F.

15. Fry only a few pieces at a time.

16. Cook for about 1 minute on the first side.

17. Turn and cook for about 1 minute on the second side, until puffed and golden.

18. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Serve immediately with cured meats, cheeses, or pickles.

Chef's note

The high frying temperature puffs the dough quickly and limits oil absorption.

title: Tigella Modenese
instructions:
Tigella Modenese

Soft Modena flatbreads enriched with lard and cooked on a tigelliera or heavy griddle.

Yield: about 14 tigelle

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp warm whole milk

about 1 1/2 tsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

2. Put the flour in a large bowl.

3. Add the warm milk.

4. Add the yeast water.

5. Knead for 3–4 minutes.

6. Gradually work in the softened lard.

7. Add the salt.

8. Knead for another 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

9. Form a ball.

10. Cover.

11. Let rise for about 2 hours, until nearly doubled.

12. Roll the dough about 3/8 inch thick.

13. Cut rounds 3–3 1/2 inches wide.

14. Cover the rounds and rest for 20 minutes.

15. Heat a tigelliera or heavy griddle over medium heat.

16. Cook the tigelle for about 3 minutes on the first side.

17. Turn.

18. Cook for another 2–3 minutes, until golden and cooked through.

19. Keep cooked tigelle under a clean kitchen towel.

title: Coppia Ferrarese
instructions:
Coppia Ferrarese

Firm Ferrara bread enriched with lard and malt, shaped into the traditional four-pointed paired loaf.

Yield: 4 paired loaves

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
scant 1 cup warm water
3 1/2 tbsp softened lard
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp barley malt or honey

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast and malt in the warm water.

2. Put the flour in a bowl.

3. Gradually add the yeast water.

4. Knead for 5 minutes.

5. Add the softened lard in small portions.

6. Add the salt.

7. Continue kneading for 10–12 minutes.

8. The dough should be fairly firm, smooth, and elastic.

9. Cover and rest for about 60 minutes.

10. Divide into 8 equal pieces.

11. Stretch each piece into a strip.

12. Roll and taper each strip to create a thicker center and pointed end.

13. Join two pieces at the center, crossing them slightly, to form one loaf with four points.

14. Repeat with the remaining dough.

15. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

16. Cover and proof for 30–40 minutes without letting the loaves overproof.

17. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

18. Bake on the center rack for 25–30 minutes, until evenly golden.

19. Cool on a rack.

Chef's note

Coppia Ferrarese requires firm dough; excess hydration causes the characteristic pointed ends to lose their definition.

title: Pane di Pavullo
instructions:
Pane di Pavullo

Modena mountain bread made with white and whole-wheat flour, natural starter, and lard.

Preparation

1. Dissolve the sourdough starter in the warm water.

2. Add the salt and stir.

3. Combine the two flours in a large bowl.

4. Gradually add the starter mixture.

5. Add the melted but cooled lard.

6. Knead thoroughly for about 12–15 minutes, until smooth and cohesive.

7. Form a ball.

8. Cover with a cloth.

9. Let rise for about 8 hours in a draft-free place.

10. Dust the work surface with the measured flour.

11. Turn out the dough gently.

12. Shape into a round loaf or bâtard without aggressively deflating it.

13. Put it on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

14. Cover and rise for another 1 1/2–2 hours.

15. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

16. Score the surface.

17. Bake for 15 minutes at 425°F.

18. Reduce the oven to 400°F.

19. Bake for another 25–30 minutes.

20. Cool completely on a rack.

Chef's note

Traditional dough is fairly firm. Keeping the water close to 40% of the flour weight produces the characteristic compact crumb.

Micca Parmigiana

Parma-style lard-enriched loaf with a golden crust and soft crumb.

Yield: 1 loaf, about 1 7/8 lb

Preparation

1. Pour about 1 1/4 cups water into a bowl.

2. Dissolve the yeast in it.

3. Gradually add the flour.

4. Mix until no dry flour remains.

5. Rest for 15 minutes.

6. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon water.

7. Gradually work in the salted water.

8. Add the softened lard in 2–3 additions.

9. Knead for 8–10 minutes, until smooth.

10. Form a ball.

11. Cover.

12. Let rise for about 2 hours.

13. Dust the work surface with the measured flour.

14. Shape the loaf gently.

15. Put it on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

16. Cover.

17. Rise for 45–60 minutes.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

20. Bake for 15 minutes at 425°F.

Adding the lard only after the initial rest lets the flour hydrate before fat coats the proteins.

title: Chisola Piacentina
instructions:
Chisola Piacentina

Val Tidone focaccia enriched with pork cracklings, lard, and dry white wine.

Yield: 1 large focaccia, 6 servings

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
1 cup warm water, divided
about 2 tbsp plus 1 tsp fresh yeast
about 1 2/3 cups fresh pork cracklings, cut into 3/8-inch pieces
3 1/2 tbsp lard
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp dry white wine
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the pan and top

Preparation

1. Measure 3/4 cup plus 1 tablespoon flour from the total.

2. Dissolve about 1 tablespoon fresh yeast in 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon warm water.

3. Mix with the measured flour to form a small starter dough.

4. Cover and ferment for about 2 hours, until very puffy.

5. Dissolve the remaining yeast in 1/4 cup of the remaining water.

6. Put the cracklings in a skillet with about 1 1/2 tablespoons lard and 2 tablespoons water.

7. Cook over low heat for 5–7 minutes.

8. Cool completely.

9. Put the remaining flour in a bowl.

10. Add the starter dough, dissolved yeast, and wine.

11. Gradually add the remaining water.

12. Work in the remaining lard.

13. Add the salt.

14. Knead for 8–10 minutes.

15. Fold in the cooled cracklings.

16. Cover and rest for about 1 hour.

17. Grease a baking pan with half of the olive oil.

18. Spread the dough at least 5/8 inch thick.

19. Cover.

20. Rise until it increases about 3/8 inch in height, about 45–60 minutes.

21. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

22. Brush the top with the remaining olive oil.

23. Bake for about 30 minutes, until golden.

24. Cool for 10 minutes.

Chef's note

Cool the cracklings completely before adding them so their hot rendered fat does not weaken the dough structure.

title: Genoese Focaccia

Genoese Focaccia

Thin soft Genoese focaccia with deep dimples and a water, olive-oil, and salt brine.

Yield: one large baking pan, about 16 inches wide

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour

2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

1 tsp sugar

For the topping
1/4 cup water
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp coarse salt

Preparation

1. Measure 3 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon water from the total.

2. Dissolve the yeast and sugar in it.

3. Put the flour in a large bowl.

4. Add the yeast water.

5. Gradually add the remaining water.

6. Knead for 5 minutes.

7. Work in the olive oil.

8. Add the salt.

9. Continue kneading until very soft but uniform.

10. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

11. Generously oil a baking pan about 16 inches wide.

12. Transfer the dough to the pan.

13. Rest for 10 minutes.

14. Gently stretch it with your fingertips to cover the pan.

15. Mix the topping water, olive oil, and coarse salt.

16. Pour the brine over the focaccia.

17. Press your fingertips deeply into the dough to make the characteristic dimples without puncturing the bottom.

18. Cover.

19. Let rise for about 1 hour.

20. Preheat a conventional oven to 375°F.

21. Bake for 15–20 minutes, until golden on top.

22. Rest for 5 minutes.

23. Remove from the pan and cool on a rack.

Chef's note

The brine should pool in the dimples; that is what keeps the surface glossy, savory, and tender.

instructions:
Focaccia di Recco with Cheese

Ultra-thin unleavened Recco focaccia made from two delicate sheets enclosing abundant fresh crescenza.

Yield: about 10 servings

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp strong all-purpose or bread flour
1 cup plus 1 tbsp room-temperature water
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus 2 tbsp for the pan and top
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
about 4 cups fresh crescenza

Preparation

1. Put the flour and salt in a bowl.

2. Add the olive oil.

3. Gradually add the water.

4. Knead for 10–12 minutes, until soft, smooth, and elastic.

5. Divide into two equal pieces.

6. Form two balls.

7. Lightly brush with oil.

8. Cover.

9. Rest for at least 30 minutes.

10. Grease a large copper or metal baking pan with half of the finishing oil.

11. Roll the first piece with a rolling pin.

12. Lift it onto your knuckles and gently stretch until nearly transparent.

13. Line the pan, letting the dough hang over the edges.

14. Scatter small pieces of crescenza evenly over the surface.

15. Stretch the second piece in the same way, making it even thinner.

16. Lay it over the cheese.

17. Press the two dough edges together firmly.

18. Trim away excess dough.

19. Pinch small holes about 3/8 inch wide in several places across the top sheet.

20. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

21. Preheat the oven as hot as possible, ideally 520–570°F.

22. In a very hot professional oven, bake for 4–7 minutes, until blistered and golden with fully melted cheese.

23. In a home oven limited to 480°F, bake on the highest rack for about 8–10 minutes.

Service

Cut and serve immediately.

Chef's note

The pastry sheets should be nearly transparent; extreme thinness and very high heat distinguish Recco focaccia from ordinary yeasted focaccia.

Focaccia di Voltri

Voltri-style focaccia with a highly hydrated dough, deep dimples, brine, and coarse salt.

Yield: 6–8 servings

For the dough
4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
1 1/2 cups room-temperature water

1 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil

2. Put the flour in a bowl.

3. Add the yeast water.

4. Gradually add the remaining water.

5. Knead until soft and uniform.

6. Work in the olive oil.

7. Add the salt.

8. Knead for another 5 minutes.

9. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.

10. Perform one set of folds by bringing the edges of the dough toward the center.

11. Cover and rest for another 15 minutes.

12. Repeat a second set of folds.

13. Cover and rise for about 1 hour, until well puffed.

14. Grease a baking pan with some of the topping oil.

15. Transfer the dough to the pan.

16. Gently stretch it with your fingertips.

17. Rest for 20 minutes.

18. Mix the water, remaining olive oil, and fine salt to make the brine.

19. Press deep dimples into the dough with your fingertips.

20. Pour the brine over the surface.

Genoese Onion Focaccia

For the dough
2 cups strong bread flour
2/3 cup water

3 tbsp plus 1 tsp water
1/2 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp plus 2 tsp extra-virgin olive oil

For finishing
about 3 cups thinly sliced white onions

2 tsp extra-virgin olive oil for the pan

Preparation

1. Put the flour, yeast, malt, and water in a mixer or bowl.

2. Knead until the dough begins becoming elastic.

3. Add the olive oil.

4. Add the salt last.

5. Knead until smooth.

6. Shape into a slightly flattened rectangle.

7. Cover.

8. Rest on the work surface for 30 minutes.

9. Grease an 8-by-12-inch pan with the measured olive oil.

10. Transfer the dough to the pan.

11. Partially stretch it with your fingertips.

12. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

13. Stretch again until it covers the whole pan.

14. Cover and rise for 1 hour.

15. Meanwhile, thinly slice the onions.

16. Toss them with the finishing salt.

17. Rest for 30 minutes.

18. Squeeze lightly to remove excess moisture.

19. Mix the brine water and salt.

20. Add the olive oil.

21. Press dimples into the focaccia with your fingertips.

22. Pour over the brine.

23. Rise for another hour.

25. Spread the onions over the surface.

Pan Martin

4 cups plus 2 tbsp wheat or bread flour
2 1/2 cups warm water

Preparation

2. Measure 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon of the warm water.

3. Dissolve the yeast in it.

4. Pour the yeast mixture into the center of the flours.

5. Gradually add the remaining water.

6. Knead until soft, uniform, and shapeable.

7. Add the salt.

8. Continue kneading for 8–10 minutes.

9. Form a large, fairly low round loaf.

11. Put the loaf in the pan.

Piedmont Micca

2. Put the flour in a bowl.

3. Gradually add the yeast water.

4. Add the olive oil.

6. Add the salt.

7. Continue kneading until smooth and elastic.

9. Put the dough inside.

11. Refrigerate for about 12 hours.

The long cold fermentation develops flavor with very little yeast and gives the crumb greater aroma.

instructions:
Biova Piemontese

Light Piedmont bread shaped by two successive rolls, with a thin crust and dry tender crumb.

Yield: 2 large loaves

Ingredients

8 cups plus 1/3 cup all-purpose flour
2 1/2 cups warm water
about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast
2 tbsp plus 2 tsp oil
2 tsp barley malt
1 tbsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the flour, malt, and oil in a large bowl.

2. Warm the water.

3. Dissolve the yeast in it.

4. Gradually add the yeast water to the flour.

5. Knead until combined.

6. Add the salt.

7. Continue kneading until smooth.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise for 1 hour.

10. Divide the dough into two pieces.

11. Roll each portion into a long strip.

12. Roll the strip tightly onto itself.

13. Rotate the roll 90 degrees.

14. Roll it out lengthwise again.

15. Roll it up a second time.

16. Put the loaves on a floured kitchen towel, separating them with folds of fabric.

17. Cover.

18. Rise for 1 hour.

19. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

20. Transfer carefully to a parchment-lined baking sheet.

21. Score each loaf deeply lengthwise.

22. Bake for 25–30 minutes.

23. Cool on a rack.

Chef's note

The double rolling builds internal layers and helps the loaf open along the score during baking.

Torinese Stretched Breadsticks

1. Put the flour, water, olive oil, and yeast in a bowl.

2. Knead until smooth and well developed.

3. Add the salt near the end of kneading.

4. Shape into a rectangle.

5. Roll to about 5/8 inch thick.

6. Brush with the measured finishing olive oil.

7. Cover.

8. Rise for 1 hour.

9. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

10. Cut the dough into narrow strips.

11. Hold one strip by both ends.

12. Gently stretch it almost to the width of the baking sheet without rolling it on the counter.

13. Put it on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

14. Repeat with the remaining strips.

15. Bake for about 15 minutes, until dry and golden.

16. Cool completely on a rack.

Chef's note

Stretched grissini are not rolled on the counter; their irregular thin shape comes from stretching each strip between the hands.

4. Add the salt.

5. Continue until smooth, with a final dough temperature around 75–77°F.

6. Shape into one or more low wide logs.

7. Lightly oil a board or pan with some of the finishing oil.

8. Put the logs on the oiled surface.

9. Brush the tops with the remaining oil.

10. Cover.

11. Rise for about 30 minutes.

12. Cut the log into narrow strips.

13. Roll each strip under your palms into an even breadstick.

14. Arrange on parchment-lined baking sheets.

15. Cover.

16. Rise for another 60–80 minutes.

17. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

18. Bake for about 12 minutes, until dry and golden.

19. Cool completely.

Unlike stretched grissini, rubatà are deliberately rolled on the work surface, producing a more regular shape and rustic exterior.

Piedmont dark rye bread made with a long-fermented pre-dough.

Preparation

1. For the pre-dough, warm the water slightly.

2. Dissolve the yeast in it.

3. Rest for 10 minutes.

4. Add both pre-dough flours.

5. Mix briefly.

6. Cover with plastic wrap.

7. Ferment in a turned-off oven for 16–20 hours.

8. Put the pre-dough, final-dough flours, yeast, and malt in a mixer.

9. Gradually add the water.

10. Knead with the dough hook.

11. After 5 minutes, add the salt.

12. Continue until the total mixing time reaches about 20 minutes.

13. Shape into a round, fairly low loaf.

14. Put it on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

15. Cover with a cloth.

16. Rise for about 6 hours.

17. Preheat a conventional oven to 375°F.

18. Make three cuts across the top.

19. Bake for 40 minutes.

Rye develops little gluten, so the dough remains stickier and the loaf naturally flatter than all-wheat bread.

Preparation

1. Pour about 1 2/3 cups warm water into a bowl.

2. Add the yeast and optional honey.

3. Stir.

4. Rest for 5 minutes.

5. Mix the rye flour and wheat flour.

6. Gradually add the yeast water to the flours.

7. Knead for 5 minutes.

8. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon water.

9. Work in the salted water.

10. Knead for another 5–7 minutes without adding more flour.

11. Cover.

12. Rise for about 90 minutes, until visibly expanded.

13. Dust the work surface with some of the measured rye flour.

14. Shape gently into a loaf.

15. Put it on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

16. Dust the top with the remaining rye flour.

17. Cover.

18. Rise for 45–60 minutes.

19. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

20. Score the surface.

21. Bake for 15 minutes at 425°F.

22. Reduce the oven to 400°F.

Do not dry the dough with extra flour. Rye absorbs water slowly and naturally produces a stickier dough than wheat.

Preparation

2. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

3. Add the milk.

4. Pour the liquids into the flour.

5. Mix until smooth.

6. Cover and rest for 15 minutes.

7. Add the remaining 1 cup flour.

8. Add the cornstarch.

9. Add the egg yolk.

10. Add the sugar and salt.

11. Gradually work in the softened butter.

12. Knead until smooth, resilient, and elastic.

13. Cover and rest for another 15 minutes.

14. Divide into 6 equal portions.

15. Shape into smooth balls.

16. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Cover loosely with plastic wrap.

18. Rise for at least 30 minutes.

21. Sprinkle evenly with the sugar.

22. Bake for 10–12 minutes, until deeply golden.

The first short rest lets the yeast become active before the butter and sugar are added, since enriched dough rises more slowly.

instructions:
Miccone Pavese

Firm Pavia bread made with a long-fermented biga, shaped into large twisted loaves and baked without steam.

Yield: 2 large loaves

For the biga
6 2/3 cups type 0 or bread flour
1 2/3 cups water
about 1 1/2 tsp crumbled fresh yeast

For the final dough
all of the biga
1 2/3 cups type 0 or bread flour
scant 1/2 cup water
about 1/2 tsp crumbled fresh yeast
1 tsp barley malt
1 tbsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Make the biga by mixing the flour with the water and yeast.

2. Mix only until no dry flour remains; the biga should stay rough rather than smooth.

3. Cover.

4. Ferment for 18 hours at about 64°F.

5. Put the biga in a mixer bowl.

6. Add the final flour, remaining yeast, malt, and about 6 tablespoons of the water.

7. Knead until the dough comes together.

8. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon water.

9. Work in the salted water.

10. Knead for several minutes until firm but elastic.

11. Cover.

12. Rest for 30 minutes.

13. Divide into two equal pieces.

14. Roll each piece into a rope about 24 inches long.

15. Fold and twist each rope over itself to make a large compact braid.

16. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Cover.

18. Rise for 1 1/2 hours.

19. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

20. Make a deep lengthwise score in each loaf.

21. Bake without steam.

22. Bake for 20 minutes at 425°F.

23. Reduce the oven to 400°F.

24. Bake for another 20 minutes.

Miccone is intentionally low-hydration; the firm dough creates its compact crumb and exceptional keeping quality.

Schüttelbrot

Very thin, crisp South Tyrolean rye bread flavored with fennel, caraway, coriander, and anise.

2. Add the rye flour.

3. Mix until uniform.

6. For the final dough, measure 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon from the water.

7. Dissolve the remaining yeast in it.

8. Put the pre-dough in a large bowl.

9. Add the rye flour, wheat flour, dissolved yeast, salt, and spices.

11. Mix vigorously with a wooden spoon; the dough should remain very soft.

22. Transfer to the baking sheet.

Pusterer Breatl

Small Puster Valley loaves made with rye, wheat, yeast, and traditional bread spices.

instructions:
South Tyrolean Rye Bread

South Tyrolean rye bread with a long pre-ferment and caraway, fennel, coriander, and fenugreek.

Yield: 3 loaves

For the pre-ferment
1 3/4 cups plus 1 tbsp rye flour
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp water

3 cups rye flour
3 1/3 cups type 0 or bread flour
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp ground caraway seeds
1 tsp ground fennel seeds
1 tsp ground coriander seeds
1 tsp ground fenugreek seeds
1/4 cup rye flour for the work surface

Preparation

1. Quickly mix the pre-ferment rye flour, water, and yeast.

2. Cover with plastic wrap.

3. Ferment for 12 hours at room temperature.

4. Put the pre-ferment in a mixer bowl.

5. Add all final-dough ingredients except the work-surface flour.

6. Knead with the dough hook for 10 minutes.

7. Cover the bowl.

8. Rise for 1 hour in a warm place.

9. Dust the work surface generously with rye flour.

10. Weigh the dough and divide into 3 equal pieces.

11. Pat each piece into a rectangle about 8 by 6 inches.

12. Fold the two far corners toward the center.

13. Roll the rectangle firmly toward you.

14. Put the roll seam-side down on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

15. Repeat with the other two pieces.

16. Cover.

17. Rise for 1 hour.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

19. Spray a small amount of water onto the oven walls when loading the bread to create steam.

20. Bake for about 45 minutes.

21. Cool completely on a rack.

Chef's note

The dough should remain slightly sticky; this is normal for bread with a high proportion of rye.

Ur-paarl

Val Venosta paired bread made with rye, whole spelt, sourdough, and Alpine bread spices.

1 1/4 cups warm water at about 95°F
about 3/4 cup active rye sourdough starter
1 1/4 cups whole-spelt flour
3 cups whole-rye flour
1/2 tsp ground fenugreek
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp crushed coriander
3/4 tsp fennel seeds
1/2 tsp caraway seeds
2 tbsp spelt flour for dusting

Preparation

1. Warm the water to about 95°F.

2. Mix it with the sourdough starter until dispersed.

3. Add the spelt and rye flours.

4. Add the fenugreek, salt, coriander, fennel, and caraway.

5. Mix and knead until soft and uniform.

6. Cover.

7. Rise for 20 minutes at about 95°F.

8. Knead again for 1–2 minutes.

9. Divide into 4 portions for two large paired loaves, or 8 portions for four smaller pairs.

10. Shape into low round disks.

11. Set them together in pairs so the edges just touch.

12. Dust with the spelt flour.

13. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

14. Cover.

15. Rise for another 20 minutes.

16. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

17. Bake for 15 minutes.

18. Reduce the oven to 340°F.

19. Bake for another 25 minutes.

20. Cool on a rack.

Chef's note

The traditional shape comes from joining two small disks; do not press them together, because proofing naturally fuses the pair.

instructions:
Molche Bread

Garda Trentino bread enriched with molche, the olive paste left from olive-oil pressing.

Yield: 2 loaves

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 1 or all-purpose flour
1/2 cup plus 2 tsp water
1/2 cup whole milk
1 tsp active dry yeast or about 2 1/4 tsp fresh yeast
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
about 3/4 cup molche olive paste
2 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp flour for the work surface

Preparation

1. Put the flour, yeast, water, milk, olive oil, and molche in the mixer bowl.

2. Knead for 8 minutes.

3. Add the salt.

4. Knead for another minute.

5. Dust the work surface with the measured flour.

6. Turn out the dough.

7. Perform two complete folds.

8. Form a ball.

9. Put it in a bowl.

10. Cover.

11. Rise for 1 hour.

12. Divide the dough into two pieces.

13. Roll each piece onto itself.

14. Rest for 5 minutes.

15. Gently lengthen into two loaves.

16. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Cover.

18. Rise for 70 minutes.

19. Preheat a conventional oven to 480°F with a small metal pan on the bottom rack.

20. Score the loaves.

21. Pour a scant 1/2 cup boiling water into the lower pan to create steam.

22. Load the bread.

23. Immediately reduce the oven to 425°F.

24. Bake for 30 minutes.

25. Cool completely on a rack.

Chef's note

Molche already contributes fat and savoriness, so adding it from the beginning distributes it evenly throughout the dough.

instructions:
Pan de Siór

Veneto festive bread from Sanguinetto packed with nuts, dark chocolate, raisins, fennel seeds, and Sassolino liqueur.

Yield: 1 large sweet loaf, about 16 servings

Ingredients

8 1/3 cups all-purpose flour
10 1/2 tbsp butter, melted and cooled
2 large eggs
2 tbsp plus 2 tsp Sassolino liqueur
2 tbsp plus 2 tsp baking powder
about 2/3 cup coarsely grated dark chocolate
1 1/4 cups coarsely chopped walnuts
1 1/4 cups coarsely chopped almonds
1/3 cup pine nuts
1/3 cup raisins
1/3 cup fennel seeds
2 tsp butter for the pan
1 tbsp flour for the pan
2 tbsp plus 1 tsp sugar for finishing

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

2. Drain and dry very thoroughly.

3. Preheat a conventional oven to 350°F.

4. Butter and flour a large baking pan or mold.

5. Put the flour in a large bowl.

6. Add the baking powder.

7. Pour in the cooled melted butter.

8. Add the eggs and Sassolino.

9. Mix until a compact, uniform dough forms.

10. Add the grated chocolate.

11. Fold in the walnuts, almonds, pine nuts, raisins, and fennel seeds.

12. Mix only until the additions are evenly distributed.

13. Shape into one large, slightly flattened ball.

14. Put it in the prepared pan.

15. Rest for 1 hour.

16. Bake for about 60 minutes.

17. Test the center with a skewer; it should come out without raw dough.

18. Cool completely.

19. Sprinkle with the finishing sugar before serving.

Chef's note

Chop the nuts coarsely rather than grinding them into meal so the bread keeps its traditional rustic texture.

South Tyrolean Schüttelbrot

Ultra-thin crisp South Tyrolean rye bread flavored with fennel, caraway, and fenugreek.

Yield: about 12 flatbreads

2 cups plus 1 tbsp rye flour
1 cup plus 1 tbsp water at about 86°F

4 cups plus 2 tbsp rye flour
2 cups wheat flour

about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp ground fennel
1 tsp ground caraway

1/3 cup rye flour for handling

Preparation

1. Dissolve the pre-dough yeast in the warm water.

2. Add the rye flour.

3. Mix into a soft uniform mass.

4. Cover.

5. Ferment for 1 hour at about 86°F.

6. Put the pre-dough in a large bowl.

7. Add the rye flour, wheat flour, yeast, salt, fennel, caraway, and fenugreek.

8. Gradually add the water.

9. Mix vigorously until very soft.

10. Cover.

11. Rest for 10–15 minutes.

12. Dust the work surface generously with rye flour.

13. Divide the dough into portions of about 1 cup each.

14. Shape into small rounds.

15. Put them on floured kitchen towels.

16. Rest for 10 minutes in a warm humid place.

17. Preheat a conventional oven to 420°F.

18. Put one round on a well-floured round board.

19. Shake and rotate the board with short movements until the dough spreads into a wide, very thin disk.

20. Transfer to a parchment-lined baking sheet.

21. Repeat with the remaining portions.

22. Bake for about 30 minutes, until completely dry and crisp.

23. Cool completely before storing.

Chef's note

Schüttelbrot should be thin and dry rather than soft; the characteristic shaking motion replaces rolling with a pin.

instructions:
Polesine Ciabatta

Highly hydrated Veneto ciabatta with long fermentation and an open, airy crumb.

Yield: 4 small loaves

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp strong type 0 or bread flour
1 1/2 cups room-temperature water, divided
1 tsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 tsp sugar
1/4 cup durum semolina for the work surface

Preparation

1. Pour about 1 1/3 cups water into a bowl.

2. Dissolve the yeast and sugar in it.

3. Gradually add the flour.

4. Mix until no dry flour remains.

5. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

6. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 2 tablespoons water.

7. Gradually work the salted water into the dough.

8. Add the olive oil.

9. Work for 8–10 minutes, until elastic while remaining very soft.

10. Cover.

11. Rise for about 4 hours.

12. During the first hour, perform two sets of folds 30 minutes apart.

13. Dust the work surface generously with the semolina.

14. Turn out the dough gently without deflating it.

15. Divide into 4 rectangles.

16. Gently lengthen each piece without tightening it.

17. Transfer to a parchment-lined baking sheet.

18. Cover.

19. Rise for 45–60 minutes.

20. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

21. Bake for 25–30 minutes, until deeply golden and light for their size.

22. Leave the oven door slightly ajar during the final 5 minutes to dry the crust.

23. Cool on a rack.

Chef's note

Handle the dough as little as possible after the first rise; the fermentation bubbles create ciabatta's characteristic open crumb.

title: Ciopa Vicentina
instructions:
Ciopa Vicentina

Firm Vicenza bread shaped from two small curved rolls joined side by side.

1 1/4 cups room-temperature water
about 3 tbsp dry sourdough starter
1 tsp barley malt or sugar
3/4 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp flour for the work surface

Preparation

1. Sift the flour into a bowl.

2. Add the malt and dry sourdough starter.

3. Gradually add the water.

4. Knead until smooth and fairly firm.

5. Add the salt.

6. Knead for another 5 minutes.

7. Put the dough in a bowl.

8. Cover.

9. Rise in a warm place for 4–6 hours, until doubled.

10. Dust the work surface with the measured flour.

11. Turn out the dough gently.

12. Divide into 8 equal portions.

13. Shape each portion into a small curved roll.

14. Place two rolls together side by side to form each ciopa.

15. Arrange the 4 ciope on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

16. Cover with a damp kitchen towel.

17. Rise for 1 hour.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

19. Bake for 20–30 minutes depending on size, until deeply golden.

20. Cool completely on a rack.

Chef's note

Traditional ciopa is a relatively firm bread dough; do not add extra water once it reaches a firm workable consistency.

Montasù

Veneto bread rolls shaped from two curled sections crossed over one another.

1 cup plus 2 tbsp water
1 tsp fresh yeast
1 1/2 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

1. Put about 4 cups of the flour in the mixer bowl.

2. Add the yeast and water.

3. Knead until combined.

4. Add the salt.

5. Add the olive oil.

6. Gradually add the remaining flour.

7. Knead until smooth.

8. Form a ball.

9. Cover.

10. Rest for about 2 hours.

11. Dust the work surface with the measured flour.

12. Divide the dough into pieces of about 1/2 cup each.

13. Pre-shape each piece into a short cylinder.

14. Cover and rest for 15–20 minutes.

15. Roll each piece into a long narrow tongue.

16. Fold and roll inward from both ends to create two small coils.

17. Cross the two coils in the characteristic montasù shape.

18. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

19. Cover.

20. Rise for 1 hour.

21. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

22. Bake for 18–20 minutes, until golden.

23. Cool on a rack.

Chef's note

The short rest after pre-shaping relaxes the gluten so each piece can be rolled thin without tearing.

Veneto Pan Biscotto

Very firm Veneto bread baked once and then slowly dried until crisp and friable.

Yield: about 12 small breads

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
1 3/4 tsp active dry yeast
2/3 cup room-temperature water, divided
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 1/2 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the flour and yeast in a bowl.

2. Add 1/2 cup water.

3. Knead until the flour begins coming together.

4. Work in the olive oil.

5. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 2 tablespoons water.

6. Gradually add the salted water.

7. Knead vigorously for 12–15 minutes.

8. The dough should be very firm and dry but completely cohesive.

9. Form a ball.

10. Cover.

11. Rise in a warm place until doubled, about 3–4 hours.

12. Divide into 12 portions.

13. Shape each piece into a small triangle.

14. Roll each triangle from the wide base toward the point like a small crescent.

15. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

16. Cover.

17. Rise for 30 minutes.

18. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

19. Bake for 22–25 minutes, until nearly fully baked but still relatively pale.

20. Remove the pan.

21. Reduce the oven to 250°F.

22. Wait 10 minutes for the oven temperature to fall.

23. Return the breads to the oven.

24. Dry for 35–45 minutes, turning once.

25. Turn off the oven.

26. Cool completely inside with the door slightly ajar.

Chef's note

The second bake should not significantly darken the bread; its purpose is to remove remaining moisture and create the traditional long shelf life.

title: Biga Servolana
instructions:
Biga Servolana

Trieste bread from Servola shaped in pairs and made with an overnight pre-dough and butter.

Yield: about 6 paired rolls

Ingredients

For the first dough
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
3 tbsp warm water
about 1/4 tsp fresh yeast

For the final dough
1 1/4 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
1/3 cup plus 2 tsp warm water
1 tbsp softened butter
3/4 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp flour for the work surface

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

2. Rest for 10 minutes.

3. Add the flour.

4. Knead into a small dough ball.

5. Put it in a bowl.

6. Cover.

7. Rise overnight, about 10–12 hours.

8. The next day, put the risen dough in a bowl.

9. Gradually add the final flour, alternating it with the warm water.

10. Add the salt.

11. Work in the softened butter.

12. Knead until smooth.

13. Form a dough ball.

14. Cover.

15. Rise for another 5 hours.

16. Dust the work surface with the measured flour.

17. Take pieces from the dough without re-kneading the whole mass.

18. Shape into small ovals.

19. Join the ovals in pairs.

20. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

21. Cover.

22. Rise for 30 minutes.

23. Preheat a conventional oven to 425°F.

24. Bake for 15 minutes, until lightly golden.

25. Cool on a rack.

Chef's note

After the long second rise, do not re-knead the dough; cut and shape it directly to preserve the gas already developed.

title: Pan de Frizze
instructions:
Pan de Frizze

Small Trieste breads enriched with pork cracklings, black pepper, and lard.

Yield: 8–10 small loaves

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp type 0 or all-purpose flour
1 cup plus 3 tbsp warm water
1 3/4 tsp active dry yeast or about 1 1/2 tbsp fresh yeast
about 1 1/4 cups pork cracklings
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp sugar
1 1/2 tbsp softened lard
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 tbsp flour for the work surface

Preparation

1. Measure 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon water from the total.

2. Dissolve the yeast and sugar in it.

3. Rest for 5–10 minutes.

4. Put the flour in a large bowl.

5. Add the yeast water.

6. Gradually add the remaining water.

7. Knead for 5 minutes.

8. Add the salt and pepper.

9. Work in the softened lard.

10. Add the cracklings.

11. Knead only until they are evenly distributed.

12. Form a ball.

13. Cover.

14. Rise for about 90 minutes, until well puffed.

15. Dust the work surface with the measured flour.

16. Divide into 8–10 portions.

17. Shape into small round or oval loaves.

18. Arrange on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

19. Cover.

20. Rise for 45–60 minutes.

21. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

22. Bake for 25–30 minutes, until deeply golden.

23. Cool on a rack.

Chef's note

Add the cracklings only near the end of mixing so they remain as distinct small pieces throughout the crumb.

title: Biga Friulana
instructions:
Biga Friulana

Paired Friulian rolls made with a long-fermented biga, white spelt, and lard.

Yield: about 10 paired rolls

Ingredients

For the biga
2 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
1/2 cup water
3/4 tsp fresh yeast

For the final dough
all of the biga
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp white spelt flour
1 1/4 cups type 0 or all-purpose flour
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp water, divided
1 tsp barley malt
2 tsp fine salt
3 1/2 tbsp softened lard
2 tbsp flour for dusting

Preparation

1. Mix the flour, water, and yeast for the biga until rough and shaggy.

2. Cover.

3. Ferment for 18 hours at about 64°F.

4. The next day, put the biga in a mixer.

5. Add the spelt, type 0 flour, malt, and about 2/3 cup water.

6. Knead until the dough begins becoming elastic.

7. Dissolve the salt in the remaining 2 tablespoons water.

8. Gradually add the salted water.

9. Work in the lard little by little.

10. Knead until smooth.

11. Cover.

12. Rise for 2 hours.

13. Divide into portions of about 1/2–3/4 cup each.

14. Fold the edges of each portion toward the center.

15. Turn over and shape into smooth balls.

16. Place the balls together in pairs on a parchment-lined baking sheet.

17. Cover.

18. Rise for another 2 hours.

19. Preheat a conventional oven to 465°F.

20. Score the rolls with a razor.

21. Dust lightly with the measured flour.

22. Bake for 40 minutes.

23. Cool on a rack.

Chef's note

The biga develops flavor and structure during a cool fermentation; do not speed up the 18-hour maturation with higher temperatures.
